newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 13.

text.p: Gillette Co agreed to buy Duracell International Inc for about $7.3 billion in stock, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday,
* Ford Motor Co and the United Auto Workers Union are close to reaching a contract that doubles the time it takes new workers to achieve pay parity.
* The Federal Reserve is drafting new rules intended to simply the language on automobile leases.
* Doubletree Corp agreed to acquire Red Lion Hotels for $1 billion in cash and stock.
* Tudor Investment Corp agreed to pay $800,000 in fines to settle U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission charges that it violated trading rules.
* Wholesale prices rose 0.3 percent in August.
* About 42 percent of the money in American 401(k) retirement plans are invested in the stock of the workers' employers.
* Local telephone companies are pressing the Federal Communications Commission to allow a fee to be charged when customers ask to keep a phone number after changing carriers.
* Time Warner Inc plans to lay off workers, sell assets and cut costs after completing its merger with Turner Broadcasting System Inc.
* Oracle Corp profit more than double in its first quarter.
* A former Kmart Corp official and a real-estate broker were indicted by a federal grand jury on allegations they tried to defraud the retailer.
